::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: convex-hessian-3d-r
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| eval: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of f(x) = exp(2 x1 + x2) - x1 for x1 from -1 to 1 and x2 from -3 to 3.
#|   The surface is a trough that rises steeply toward the upper right, where 2 x1 plus x2 is large, and is nearly flat on the lower left.
#|   A dashed vermilion straight line along the direction (1, -2) through the origin lies on the surface, because f is linear there.
ch3_x1_3d <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 101)
ch3_x2_3d <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101)
ch3_f_3d <- function(x1, x2) exp(2 * x1 + x2) - x1
ch3_z_3d <- outer(ch3_x2_3d, ch3_x1_3d, ch3_f_3d)
ch3_line_x1_3d <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 21)
ch3_line_x2_3d <- -2 * ch3_line_x1_3d
ch3_line_z_3d <- ch3_f_3d(ch3_line_x1_3d, ch3_line_x2_3d)
ch3_line_3d <- tibble::tibble(
  x1 = ch3_line_x1_3d,
  x2 = ch3_line_x2_3d,
  z = ch3_line_z_3d
)
ch3_dash_3d <- list(color = "#D55E00", dash = "dash", width = 5)
plotly::plot_ly() |>
  plotly::add_surface(
    x = ch3_x1_3d,
    y = ch3_x2_3d,
    z = ch3_z_3d,
    colorscale = list(c(0, 1), c("#CCE0F0", "#0072B2")),
    showscale = FALSE,
    opacity = 0.8
  ) |>
  plotly::add_trace(
    data = ch3_line_3d,
    x = ~x1,
    y = ~x2,
    z = ~z,
    type = "scatter3d",
    mode = "lines",
    line = ch3_dash_3d,
    name = "f is linear"
  ) |>
  plotly::layout(
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(title = "x1"),
      yaxis = list(title = "x2"),
      zaxis = list(title = "f(x)"),
      camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.6, y = -1.6, z = 0.9))
    ),
    legend = list(orientation = "h")
  )
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: convex-hessian-3d-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of f(x) = exp(2 x1 + x2) - x1 for x1 from -1 to 1 and x2
#|   from -3 to 3. The surface is a trough that rises steeply toward the
#|   upper right, where 2 x1 plus x2 is large, and is nearly flat on the
#|   lower left. A dashed vermilion straight line along the direction (1, -2)
#|   through the origin lies on the surface, because f is linear there.
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

ch_x1_3d, ch_x2_3d = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(-1, 1, 101),
                                 np.linspace(-3, 3, 101))
ch_z_3d = np.exp(2 * ch_x1_3d + ch_x2_3d) - ch_x1_3d
ch_line_x1_3d = np.linspace(-1, 1, 21)
ch_line_x2_3d = -2 * ch_line_x1_3d
ch_line_z_3d = np.exp(2 * ch_line_x1_3d + ch_line_x2_3d) - ch_line_x1_3d
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4.5))
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="3d")
ax.plot_surface(ch_x1_3d, ch_x2_3d, ch_z_3d, color="#0072B2", alpha=0.6)
ax.plot(ch_line_x1_3d, ch_line_x2_3d, ch_line_z_3d, "--", color="#D55E00",
        label="f is linear")
ax.set_xlabel("x1")
ax.set_ylabel("x2")
ax.set_zlabel("f(x)")
ax.legend(loc="upper right")
plt.show();
```

:::

The [graph](functions.qmd#def-graph) of the third [function](functions.qmd#def-function) in @exm-convex-hessian,
the surface whose [level curves](vector-calculus.qmd#def-level-set) are in @fig-convex-hessian.
Along the dashed line through the origin in the [direction](vector-calculus.qmd#def-direction) $\tp{(1, -2)}$ the surface is a straight line,
the function is [linear](algebra.qmd#def-linear-function) there,
so the function is [convex](algebra.qmd#def-convex-function) but not [strictly convex](#def-strictly-convex).

:::
